data.description:
Remove the deprecated force_close INPUT surface so the write-op parity oracle needs zero exceptions (operator ruling 2026-08-18: remove deprecated flags/verbs rather than exempt them). force is the sanctioned gate-bypass across all surfaces; force_close is its deprecated predecessor and must not be mirrored or allow-listed.

EVENT-SOURCING CAVEAT (critical): force_close is not only a CLI/lib input — it lives in the EVENT SCHEMA + reducer (src/rebar/schemas/ticket_state.schema.json, src/rebar/reducer/_processors_status.py, src/rebar/_commands/txn.py, transition_close.py, close_precheck.py, types.py). This is an event-sourced store: historical events carrying force_close MUST keep reducing correctly. Therefore REMOVE THE INPUT SURFACE ONLY (the lib transition(force_close=...) param and the CLI close --force spelling), routed through the supported rebar._deprecations tombstone/warn path; the reducer/schema keep tolerating historical force_close events (tombstone, NOT hard delete).

SCOPE: retire force_close as an accepted INPUT on lib + CLI via a warn-tombstone; keep reducer back-compat; confirm the force path (force=True) covers the operator use case that force_close previously served (closed-without-signature audit signal). Sweep for any other deprecated write verb/flag that would otherwise require an oracle exception.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Passing force_close as an input WARNs via rebar._deprecations and is no longer a supported param; docs no longer advertise it.
- Historical events with force_close still reduce to the same ticket state (reducer test over a fixture event carrying force_close).
- The parity oracle carries no force_close exception and still passes.
- make lint + typecheck green.
data.title: Remove deprecated force_close input surface (tombstone; keep reducer back-compat)
